title: Holi Colours
strapline: The festival of colour and spring — clouds of pink and yellow and blue, laughter, and everyone joining in together.
intent: Holi, the Hindu festival of colours, welcomes spring with joy, forgiveness and playfulness, as people throw colour and celebrate together — a burst of happiness young children instantly understand.
Honouring a real celebration from families in the community helps every child value their friends' traditions and feel proud when their own are shared.
Exploring, mixing and throwing colour (safely) is glorious sensory, creative and physical play — powders, paints, coloured water and spray.
Colour-mixing is hands-on early science and art — what happens when yellow meets blue, how colours change and blend before their eyes.
Children grow knowledge of the wider world and the language of colour and celebration — bright, mix, spring, festival, colourful, joyful.
Celebrating together with music, dancing and shared delight builds community, movement and the sense that everyone belongs in the fun.
implementation: Learn about Holi with families who celebrate it — invite them to share their traditions, and follow their lead so it is accurate and respectful.
Offer safe ways to explore colour outdoors — coloured water in spray bottles, cornflour-paint powders, chalk, painting on a big shared sheet or the ground.
Model the colour-mixing wonder: 'You've splashed yellow onto the blue — look what's happening! What colour is it turning into?'
Bring in early science and maths — mix and predict colours, sort by shade light to dark, count and name the colours you make.
Move and celebrate together — music, dancing, throwing colour, everyone joining in — so the shared joy of the festival is real.
Keep it safe and comfortable — old clothes or aprons, gentle powders, respect for children who prefer to watch, and a wash-off plan ready.
key_questions: You've splashed yellow onto the blue — what colour is it turning into?
How could we sort these colours from light to dark?
How many colours have we made together?
What happens when you mix two powders?
How does your family celebrate Holi at home?

active_learning: Children join in wholeheartedly with the shared celebration, dancing, mixing and playing together.
creating_thinking: Children predict and discover what happens when colours mix, and make sense of a festival alongside their own.
